Table~\ref{tab:main} answers the primary detection question. The proposed score did not improve observation detection over the development-selected comparator. Its paired average-precision differences were negative with intervals excluding zero in the three synthetic configurations and SKAB. The Intel interval included zero. These results favor retaining PCA as the inexpensive first detector. Nonlinear responses alone did not make the linear baseline ineffective.

There was a narrower review benefit in S32N. At 10\% screened-candidate coverage, precision was 0.906 for witness repair and 0.719 for PCA. The paired precision difference was 0.188 with interval [0.047, 0.266]. At 25\% coverage the difference was -0.037 with interval [-0.087, -0.006]. The advantage therefore concerns a limited review budget, not more complete detection. These secondary intervals are descriptive and are not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

On the same S32N candidate population, fitted-probability Brier loss was 0.049 versus 0.068 for PCA. The paired difference interval was [-0.027, -0.007]. Lower probability error does not recover faults omitted by screening. Observation screening recall ranged from 0.159 to 0.713.

Association differences all had intervals containing zero. The mask procedure supplies an inspectable alternative explanation but did not establish better association detection than direct prediction residuals. Marginally matched relation faults still had joint metadata shortcuts. The metadata-only classifier obtained ROC area 0.734 on SKAB. This limits claims about relation reasoning despite preserved degrees and attribute marginals.

Calibration had finite resolution. Intel had only 16 reference windows, so its minimum window tail was 0.059. No configuration could raise a window alarm at the nominal 1\% level. At 5\%, observed false-positive fractions for witness repair were 0.075, 0.025, 0.025, 0.000, 0.050 in table order. Figure~\ref{fig:confidence} keeps the measured families separate. The labeled probability fit and the null-tail test answer different questions.
